svg.title: The private key never crosses the wire
svg.desc: A laptop holding a 387-byte ed25519 private key and a server holding the 86-byte public key. Three numbered arrows show the server sending a challenge, the laptop signing it, and the server verifying the signature; a fourth arrow labelled 'send the private key' is crossed out in red. Below, known_hosts records the server's own key on a trust-on-first-use basis, and a port-forward runs from localhost:15432 through a bastion to a Postgres on a private subnet, with a direct route from the internet crossed out.
svg.text: The private key never crosses the wire
ed25519: keygen 0.013 s, 387 B private, 86 B public | RSA-4096: 0.380 s, 3 369 B, 730 B = 29x faster, 8.7x smaller
SIGNATURE made with the private key
server VERIFIES it with the public key
no. That is the entire point.
the other direction: the server proves ITS identity to you
the same authenticated tunnel, reused as a private wire
